question: In Gram staining, Gram-positive bacteria retain crystal violet because their thick peptidoglycan layer is completely impermeable to the acetone-alcohol decolouriser.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: The statement is actually false. The thick peptidoglycan of Gram-positive bacteria is not impermeable to the decolouriser. Instead, the acetone-alcohol dehydrates the peptidoglycan, causing it to contract and physically trap the CV-I complex. In Gram-negative bacteria, the decolouriser dissolves the thin outer LPS membrane, creating pores through which the CV-I complex escapes.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — the statement is false. The thick peptidoglycan is NOT impermeable to the decolouriser. Rather, the acetone-alcohol dehydrates the thick peptidoglycan, causing it to contract and physically trap the large crystal violet-iodine complex within the cell wall. Impermeability and physical trapping are different mechanisms.
